data.narrative:
Baykar is a private-stage defense and security company founded by Özdemir Bayraktar. The valuation analysis draws from a universe of 10 comparables: 2 public peers (DRSHF, IDEAFORGE.NS) and 8 private peers, including Anduril Industries, Helsing, Shield AI, Saronic, and Quantum-Systems.

The peer-median method proved inapplicable. While 24 same-sector peers exist in Defense & Security, filtration for stage alignment, adjacent-stage proximity, and valuation-tier similarity yielded fewer than three datapoints across all narrow buckets. A fallback to all-sector median would introduce excessive noise and obscure sector-specific dynamics, rendering the method unreliable for this analysis.

Without triangulated valuation outputs, this analysis cannot produce a quantitative range. The primary constraint is the fragmented comparability landscape: public defense-sector companies trade on different operational scales and business models than early-stage private defenseTech ventures, while the private peer set lacks sufficient homogeneity in disclosed metrics (revenue, ARR, funding stage, or valuation multiples). Key uncertainties include the absence of disclosed financial data for Baykar and its peers, heterogeneous deal structures across the private set, and the structural disconnect between public market multiples and private venture-stage risk profiles. A credible valuation would require either expanded disclosure from the peer set or reliance on alternative methods (cost-to-build, precedent transaction, or DCF) beyond the scope of this data.
